Such capital goods the exemption of which the Cabinet Secretary may determine to promote investment in the manufacturing sector: Provided that the value of such investment is not less than two billion shillings. (ix) by inserting the followi new paragraphs ng immediately after paragraph 157 - 158. Dialyzers of tariff number 8421.29.00. 159. Scrap metal. 160. Inputs or raw materials locally purchased or imported for the manufacture of pharmaceutical products upon recommendation by the Cabinet Secretary for the time being responsible for matters relating to health. 161.Bioethanol vapour (BEV) Stoves classified under HS Code 7321.12.00 ( cooking appliances and plate warmers for liquid fuel). 162. The supply of goods for the direct and exclusive use in the implementation of infrastructure projects undertaken under a public private partnership framework, upon approval by the Cabinet Secretary on the recommendation of the Cabinet Secretary for the Ministry responsible for the implementation of the project. 163. The supply of goods for direct and exclusive use in the implementation of infrastructure projects undertaken and funded by the National Infrastructure Fund as approved by the Cabinet Secretary responsible for the National Treasury. 164.Plant, machinery, equipment and spare parts imported or purchased locally for use in a project whose total investment value is not less than three billion shillings as approved by the Cabinet Secretary responsible for the National Treasury upon recommendation by the Cabinet Secretary responsible for Trade and Investment Promotion. 165. Taxable goods used in the construction of liquefied petroleum gas storage tanks and related infrastructure: Provided that the investment in the construction of liquefied petroleum gas storage tanks and related infrastructure in Kenya amounts to at least five billion shillings and upon recommendation of the Cabinet Secretary responsible for matters relating to energy. 166. The making of any advances or the granting of credit, including the sale, disposal or realization of collateral, repossessed assets or secured property arising from the enforcement of security for loans, credit or other exempt financial services. (b) in Part II- (i) in paragraph 1, by deleting subparagraph (b) and substituting therefor the following new subparagraph- (b) the issue, transfer, receipt and other dealing with money, including money transfer services, and accepting over the counter payments of household bills, but does not include- (i) the services of carriage of cash restocking of cash machines, sorting or counting money; and (ii) payment processing, settlement, merchant acqumng, gateway, aggregation services supplied over a software or platform for a fee or commission by a payment service provider: For the purpose of this paragraph- "payment service provider" means- (a) a person, company or organization which owns, possess, operates, manages or controls a public switched network for the provision of payment services; or (b) any other person, company or organization that processes or stores data on behalf of such payment service provider or users of such payment services. (ii) paragraph 25 is amended by inserting the following new definitions- For the purposes of this paragraph­ "tour operator" means a tour or safari operator licensed as such by the competent authority responsible for regulating and overseeing the tourism sector; and "in-house supplies" means supplies made from a tour operator's own resources; or bought from third parties but materially altered so that the supply made is substantially different to that purchased. (iii) by deleting paragraph 26; (iv) by inserting the following new paragraph immediately after paragraph 38- 39. The supply of services for the direct and exclusive use in the implementation of infrastructure projects undertaken under a public private partnership framework, upon approval by the Cabinet Secretary on the recommendation of the Cabinet Secretary for the Ministry responsible for the implementation of the project. 40. Taxable services used in the construction of liquefied petroleum gas storage tanks and related infrastructure: Provided that the investment in the construction of liquefied petroleum gas storage tanks and related infrastructure in Kenya amounts to at least five billion shillings and has been recommended by the Cabinet Secretary responsible for matters relating to energy .

explanation.en: This section changes the list of VAT-exempt goods and services in the First Schedule. In Part 1 (goods), paragraphs 49, 58, 62 and 109 are deleted. Paragraph 51 now also covers spare parts, and a spare parts exemption granted before 30 June 2026 continues until the project ends. In paragraph 89, the words "any other aircraft spare" become "aircraft", and in paragraph 99(i), "three hundred" becomes "two thousand". Paragraph 146 is replaced: it now covers capital goods that the Cabinet Secretary decides to exempt to promote manufacturing investment, where the investment is at least two billion shillings. New exempt goods are: dialyzers (tariff 8421.29.00); scrap metal; inputs or raw materials, bought locally or imported, for making pharmaceutical products, on the health Cabinet Secretary's recommendation; bioethanol vapour stoves (HS 7321.12.00); goods used directly and only for public private partnership infrastructure projects, once the Cabinet Secretary approves; goods used directly and only for projects funded by the National Infrastructure Fund, as approved by the Treasury Cabinet Secretary; plant, machinery, equipment and spare parts for a project with total investment of at least three billion shillings, approved by the Treasury Cabinet Secretary on the trade and investment Cabinet Secretary's recommendation; taxable goods for building liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) storage tanks and related infrastructure, where the investment in Kenya is at least five billion shillings and the energy Cabinet Secretary recommends it; and making advances or granting credit, including selling collateral, repossessed assets or secured property when a lender enforces security for loans, credit or other exempt financial services. In Part II (services), paragraph 1(b) is replaced. Dealing in money, including money transfer services and accepting over-the-counter payments of household bills, stays exempt. Carrying cash, restocking cash machines, and sorting or counting money are not exempt. Payment processing, settlement, merchant acquiring, gateway and aggregation services that a payment service provider supplies over a software or platform for a fee or commission are also not exempt. A payment service provider is a person or organization that owns or runs a public switched network for payment services, or one that processes or stores data for such a provider or its users. Paragraph 25 gets two definitions: a tour operator is a tour or safari operator licensed by the tourism sector regulator, and in-house supplies are supplies made from the operator's own resources, or bought from others but changed so much that the supply is substantially different. Paragraph 26 is deleted. Two new exempt services are added: services used directly and only for public private partnership infrastructure projects, with Cabinet Secretary approval (paragraph 39), and taxable services for building LPG storage tanks and related infrastructure, with the same five billion shilling investment and energy Cabinet Secretary recommendation (paragraph 40).
explanation.sw: Sehemu hii inabadilisha orodha ya bidhaa na huduma zisizotozwa VAT (zilizosamehewa) katika Jedwali la Kwanza. Katika Sehemu ya 1 (bidhaa), aya ya 49, 58, 62 na 109 zinafutwa. Aya ya 51 sasa inajumuisha pia vipuri, na msamaha wa vipuri uliotolewa kabla ya tarehe 30 Juni 2026 unaendelea hadi mradi ukamilike. Katika aya ya 89, maneno "any other aircraft spare" yanabadilishwa kuwa "aircraft", na katika aya ya 99(i), "three hundred" inakuwa "two thousand". Aya ya 146 inabadilishwa: sasa inahusu bidhaa za mtaji ambazo Waziri (Cabinet Secretary) ataamua kuzisamehe ili kuhimiza uwekezaji katika utengenezaji bidhaa, ikiwa thamani ya uwekezaji ni angalau shilingi bilioni mbili. Bidhaa mpya zilizosamehewa ni: dialyzers (namba ya ushuru 8421.29.00); vyuma chakavu; malighafi zinazonunuliwa humu nchini au kuagizwa kutoka nje kwa ajili ya kutengeneza dawa, kwa mapendekezo ya Waziri wa Afya; jiko la bioethanol vapour (HS 7321.12.00); bidhaa zinazotumika moja kwa moja na kwa kipekee katika miradi ya miundombinu ya ubia wa umma na sekta binafsi, Waziri akiidhinisha; bidhaa zinazotumika moja kwa moja na kwa kipekee katika miradi inayofadhiliwa na Mfuko wa Kitaifa wa Miundombinu, kwa idhini ya Waziri wa Hazina; mitambo, vifaa na vipuri vya mradi wenye uwekezaji wa angalau shilingi bilioni tatu, kwa idhini ya Waziri wa Hazina kwa mapendekezo ya Waziri wa Biashara na Kukuza Uwekezaji; bidhaa zinazotozwa ushuru zinazotumika kujenga matangi ya kuhifadhi gesi ya kupikia (LPG) na miundombinu inayohusiana, ikiwa uwekezaji nchini ni angalau shilingi bilioni tano na Waziri wa Nishati amependekeza; na utoaji wa mikopo au advansi, pamoja na kuuza dhamana, mali iliyotwaliwa au mali iliyowekwa rehani benki inapotekeleza dhamana ya mikopo au huduma nyingine za kifedha zilizosamehewa. Katika Sehemu ya II (huduma), aya ya 1(b) inabadilishwa. Shughuli za fedha, ikiwemo huduma za kutuma pesa na kupokea malipo ya bili za nyumbani kwenye kaunta, zinabaki zimesamehewa. Usafirishaji wa fedha taslimu, kujaza pesa kwenye mashine za ATM, na kupanga au kuhesabu pesa hazijasamehewa. Huduma za kuchakata malipo, kusuluhisha malipo, merchant acquiring, gateway na aggregation zinazotolewa kupitia programu au jukwaa kwa ada au kamisheni na mtoa huduma za malipo pia hazijasamehewa. Mtoa huduma za malipo ni mtu au shirika linalomiliki au kuendesha mtandao wa umma wa huduma za malipo, au anayechakata au kuhifadhi data kwa niaba ya mtoa huduma huyo au watumiaji wake. Aya ya 25 inapata fasili mbili: tour operator ni mwendeshaji wa utalii au safari aliyepewa leseni na mamlaka ya kudhibiti sekta ya utalii, na in-house supplies ni huduma zinazotolewa kutoka rasilimali zake mwenyewe, au zilizonunuliwa kutoka kwa wengine lakini zikabadilishwa kiasi kwamba zinatofautiana sana na zilizonunuliwa. Aya ya 26 inafutwa. Huduma mpya mbili zinaongezwa kwenye orodha ya msamaha: huduma zinazotumika moja kwa moja na kwa kipekee katika miradi ya miundombinu ya ubia wa umma na sekta binafsi, Waziri akiidhinisha (aya ya 39), na huduma zinazotozwa ushuru za kujenga matangi ya LPG na miundombinu inayohusiana, kwa masharti yale yale ya uwekezaji wa shilingi bilioni tano na mapendekezo ya Waziri wa Nishati (aya ya 40).
explanation.sheng: Section hii inabadilisha list ya goods na services ambazo ni exempt from VAT kwa First Schedule. Kwa Part 1 (goods), paragraphs 49, 58, 62 na 109 zina-be deleted. Paragraph 51 sasa inajumuisha pia spare parts, na exemption ya spare parts iliyopewa before 30 June 2026 inaendelea mpaka project iishe. Kwa paragraph 89, words "any other aircraft spare" zina-change kuwa "aircraft", na kwa paragraph 99(i), "three hundred" inakuwa "two thousand". Paragraph 146 ina-be replaced: sasa ni capital goods ambazo Cabinet Secretary ataamua ziwe exempt ili ku-promote investment kwa manufacturing, kama investment ni at least two billion shillings. Goods mpya zilizo exempt ni: dialyzers (tariff 8421.29.00); scrap metal; inputs au raw materials, local au imported, za ku-manufacture pharmaceutical products, kwa recommendation ya Health Cabinet Secretary; bioethanol vapour stoves (HS 7321.12.00); goods za direct na exclusive use kwa public private partnership infrastructure projects, Cabinet Secretary akiapprove; goods za direct na exclusive use kwa projects zinazofunded na National Infrastructure Fund, kwa approval ya Treasury Cabinet Secretary; plant, machinery, equipment na spare parts za project yenye total investment ya at least three billion shillings, kwa approval ya Treasury Cabinet Secretary baada ya recommendation ya Trade and Investment Promotion Cabinet Secretary; taxable goods za ku-build liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) storage tanks na infrastructure inayohusiana, kama investment kwa Kenya ni at least five billion shillings na Energy Cabinet Secretary ame-recommend; na ku-make advances au ku-grant credit, pamoja na ku-sell collateral, repossessed assets au secured property lender anapo-enforce security ya loans, credit au exempt financial services zingine. Kwa Part II (services), paragraph 1(b) ina-be replaced. Kushughulika na money, pamoja na money transfer services na ku-accept over the counter payments za household bills, bado ni exempt. Carriage ya cash, ku-restock cash machines, na ku-sort au ku-count money si exempt. Payment processing, settlement, merchant acquiring, gateway na aggregation services zinazotolewa kupitia software au platform kwa fee au commission na payment service provider pia si exempt. Payment service provider ni mtu au organization inayomiliki au ku-run public switched network ya payment services, au anayeprocess au ku-store data kwa niaba ya provider huyo au users wake. Paragraph 25 inapata definitions mbili: tour operator ni tour au safari operator mwenye licence ya regulator wa tourism sector, na in-house supplies ni supplies zinazotoka kwa own resources za operator, au zilizonunuliwa kwa wengine lakini zika-change sana hadi ni different kabisa na zilizonunuliwa. Paragraph 26 ina-be deleted. Services mbili mpya zina-added kwa exempt list: services za direct na exclusive use kwa public private partnership infrastructure projects, Cabinet Secretary akiapprove (paragraph 39), na taxable services za ku-build LPG storage tanks na infrastructure inayohusiana, kwa conditions zile zile za five billion shillings investment na recommendation ya Energy Cabinet Secretary (paragraph 40).

clauses.heading: Amendment of Second Schedule to Cap.476.
clauses.text: 33.The Second Schedule to the Value Added Tax Act is amended in Part A- ( a) by deleting paragraph 11; (b) deleting paragraph (e) and substituting therefor the following new paragraph- (b) in paragraph 31 by inserting the words "of tariff heading 8712.00.00" immediately after the word "bicycle"; (c) deleting paragraph (f) and substituting therefor the following new paragraph- (c) in paragraph 32 by inserting the words "of tariff heading 8507 .60 .00" immediately after the word "batteries"; (d) by deleting paragraph 35.

explanation.en: This section changes Part A of the Second Schedule to the VAT Act. It removes paragraph 11 and paragraph 35 from that Part. It also adds a customs classification code (tariff heading) to two paragraphs: "of tariff heading 8712.00.00" after the word "bicycle" in paragraph 31, and "of tariff heading 8507.60.00" after the word "batteries" in paragraph 32.
explanation.sw: Kifungu hiki kinarekebisha Sehemu A ya Jedwali la Pili la Sheria ya Ushuru wa Ongezeko la Thamani (VAT). Kinafuta aya ya 11 na aya ya 35. Pia kinaongeza msimbo wa uainishaji wa bidhaa za forodha katika aya mbili: "of tariff heading 8712.00.00" baada ya neno "bicycle" katika aya ya 31, na "of tariff heading 8507.60.00" baada ya neno "batteries" katika aya ya 32.
explanation.sheng: Section 33 ina-amend Part A ya Second Schedule kwa VAT Act. Ina-delete paragraph 11 na paragraph 35. Pia ina-add tariff heading (code ya customs ya kuainisha goods) kwa paragraphs mbili: "of tariff heading 8712.00.00" baada ya word "bicycle" kwa paragraph 31, na "of tariff heading 8507.60.00" baada ya word "batteries" kwa paragraph 32.

neutral_check.note: Describes only the deletions and the added tariff heading wording, with no opinion on their effect.

clauses.heading: Amendment of the section 2 of Cap. 472.
clauses.text: 34.Section 2 of the Excise Duty Act is amended by inserting the following new definition m proper alphabetical sequence- "antique, vintage or classic vehicle" means a motor vehicle whose year of first registration is at least thirty years before the date of purchase of the motor vehicle and whose value is at least ten million shillings exclusive of depreciation.

explanation.en: Section 34 adds a new definition to section 2 of the Excise Duty Act, the part that explains the Act's terms. An "antique, vintage or classic vehicle" is a motor vehicle first registered at least thirty years before the date it is bought, and worth at least ten million shillings before any reduction for depreciation (loss of value as it gets older). The new definition goes in its alphabetical place. This section only defines the term; it does not set any tax or rate itself.
explanation.sw: Kifungu cha 34 kinaongeza ufafanuzi mpya katika kifungu cha 2 cha Sheria ya Ushuru wa Bidhaa (Excise Duty Act), kinachoeleza maana ya maneno yanayotumika katika Sheria hiyo. "Gari la kale, la zamani au la kihistoria" (antique, vintage or classic vehicle) ni gari lililosajiliwa mara ya kwanza angalau miaka thelathini kabla ya tarehe ya kulinunua, na ambalo thamani yake ni angalau shilingi milioni kumi bila kupunguzwa kwa sababu ya kushuka thamani (depreciation). Kifungu hiki kinafafanua neno hilo tu; hakiweki ushuru au kiwango chochote chenyewe.
explanation.sheng: Section 34 ina-add new definition kwa section 2 ya Excise Duty Act. Definition ni ya "antique, vintage or classic vehicle": motor vehicle ambayo first registration yake ilikuwa at least thirty years before date ya purchase, na value yake ni at least ten million shillings, without depreciation (depreciation ni value loss as the vehicle inapata old). Ni definition tu, na section hii haiseti tax wala rate yoyote.

neutral_check.note: Section is a plain definition; explained only who and what the term covers, with no opinion on its effect.

clauses.heading: Amendment of section 29 of Cap. 472.
clauses.text: 35.Section 29 of the Excise Duty Act is amended in subsection (1) by inserting the following new paragraph immediately after paragraph (b) - (c) the excise duty has been paid in respect of inputs used by a licenced or registered manufacturer to manufacture excisable goods otherwise exempt under Paragraph 12 of Part A of the Second Schedule, where the inputs are directly attributable to the manufactured goods.

explanation.en: Section 35 adds a new item (c) to the list in section 29(1) of the Excise Duty Act. The new item covers a licensed or registered manufacturer who has paid excise duty on inputs (the materials and other things used up in production) to make goods that are normally exempt under Paragraph 12 of Part A of the Second Schedule. It applies only where those inputs are directly attributable to the manufactured goods, meaning they can be traced straight to those goods.
explanation.sw: Kifungu cha 35 kinaongeza aya mpya (c) katika kifungu kidogo cha 29(1) cha Sheria ya Ushuru wa Bidhaa (Excise Duty Act). Hali hiyo mpya inahusu mtengenezaji mwenye leseni au aliyesajiliwa ambaye amelipa ushuru wa bidhaa kwa pembejeo alizotumia kutengeneza bidhaa ambazo kwa kawaida zimesamehewa ushuru huo chini ya Aya ya 12 ya Sehemu A ya Jedwali la Pili. Inahusu pembejeo zinazoweza kuhusishwa moja kwa moja na bidhaa zilizotengenezwa.
explanation.sheng: Section 35 ina-add new paragraph (c) kwa list ya section 29(1) ya Excise Duty Act. Case hiyo mpya ni ya manufacturer mwenye licence au aliye-register, ambaye amelipa excise duty kwa inputs alizotumia ku-make goods ambazo normally ni exempt chini ya Paragraph 12 ya Part A ya Second Schedule. Inahusu tu inputs ambazo ni directly attributable kwa goods hizo, yaani zinaweza ku-link straight na goods alizo-make.

neutral_check.note: Describes only what the new paragraph adds and its conditions, with no opinion, advice or judgment on legality.

explanation.en: Section 36 changes the First Schedule of the Excise Duty Act, which lists goods and services and the excise duty on each. In Part I (second table): the entry for imported gas cylinders now adds tariff code 7311.00.10. The old entry for fruit and vegetable juice is deleted and replaced by two new entries: juice with no added sugar at KSh 14.14 per litre, and juice with added sugar or other sweetener at KSh 20 per litre. The words "bottled or similarly packaged waters and other" are removed from the non-alcoholic beverages entry, so it now reads "non-alcoholic beverages, not including fruit or vegetable juices". New rates: cigars, cheroots and cigarillos, KSh 18,000 per kilogram; other manufactured tobacco and tobacco substitutes, KSh 12,550 per kilogram; imported sugar (with the existing exclusions for pharmaceutical manufacturers and licensed sugar refineries), KSh 40 per kilogram; imported ceramic sanitary fixtures (tariff 6910) and imported ceramic tiles and paving (tariff 6907), each 5% of the excisable value or KSh 50 per kilogram, whichever is higher; and extra neutral alcohol above 90% strength bought by licensed spirit makers, KSh 80 per litre. The two old entries for imported plastic articles (heading 3923.30.00, and 3923.30.00 with 3923.90.00) are deleted. In the float glass entry (tariff 7005), the exclusion for goods from East African Community Partner States that meet the EAC Rules of Origin is removed, while the exclusion for registered processors recommended by the Cabinet Secretary stays. New entries added: imported plastic articles (3923.30.00 and 3923.90.90), 10%; antique, vintage and classic vehicles, 50% of the excisable value; imported MDF, particle boards, block board, plywood and timber of tariff 4407.19.00, each 30% of the excisable value; imported unprinted banner sheeting, flex banner and unprinted PVC sheeting (3921.12.10 and 3921.90.10), KSh 200 per kilogram or 35% of the excisable value; imported shower heads (8516.10) and heating elements used only to make them, each 35%; oral smokeless tobacco such as Swedish-style snus, KSh 2,000 per kilogram; unprinted plastic sheets (3920.43.10), 10%; and pre-personal chip modules (8542.31.00), 10%. In Part II: in paragraph 4A, "deposited into a customer's betting wallet" becomes "deposited for betting purposes", and the proviso to paragraph 4A is deleted. In paragraph 4B, the same words become "deposited for gambling purposes". In paragraph 9, the word "service" is inserted before "providers". In Part III: the definition of "amount deposited into a customer's betting wallet" is deleted. A new definition of "amount deposited" is added: the total money or money's worth paid, transferred, credited or made available for betting or gambling to a person licensed under the Gambling Control Act, whether from a player or the operator, in cash or cash equivalents, whether or not held in an account, or turned into chips, tokens, tickets or credits. Definitions of "virtual asset" and "virtual asset service provider" are added, taking the meaning in section 2 of the Virtual Asset Service Providers Act, 2025.
explanation.sw: Kifungu cha 36 kinabadilisha Jedwali la Kwanza la Sheria ya Ushuru wa Bidhaa, linaloorodhesha bidhaa na huduma pamoja na ushuru wa bidhaa wa kila moja. Katika Sehemu ya I (jedwali la pili): maelezo ya mitungi ya gesi inayoagizwa kutoka nje sasa yanaongeza msimbo wa ushuru 7311.00.10. Kipengele cha zamani cha juisi ya matunda na ya mboga kinafutwa, na vipengele viwili vipya vinaingizwa: juisi isiyo na sukari iliyoongezwa, KSh 14.14 kwa lita, na juisi yenye sukari au kitamu kilichoongezwa, KSh 20 kwa lita. Maneno "bottled or similarly packaged waters and other" yanaondolewa kwenye kipengele cha vinywaji visivyo na kileo, hivyo sasa kinasomeka "non-alcoholic beverages, not including fruit or vegetable juices". Viwango vipya ni: sigara za cigar, cheroot na cigarillo, KSh 18,000 kwa kilo; tumbaku nyingine iliyotengenezwa na mbadala wake, KSh 12,550 kwa kilo; sukari inayoagizwa kutoka nje (isipokuwa ile ya watengenezaji wa dawa na viwanda vya kusafisha sukari vyenye leseni), KSh 40 kwa kilo; vifaa vya usafi vya kauri vinavyoagizwa (aina ya 6910) na vigae vya kauri vinavyoagizwa (aina ya 6907), kila kimoja asilimia 5 ya thamani inayotozwa ushuru au KSh 50 kwa kilo, kutegemea kiasi kikubwa zaidi; na pombe ya extra neutral alcohol yenye nguvu zaidi ya asilimia 90 inayonunuliwa na watengenezaji wenye leseni, KSh 80 kwa lita. Vipengele viwili vya zamani vya bidhaa za plastiki zinazoagizwa (3923.30.00, na 3923.30.00 pamoja na 3923.90.00) vinafutwa. Katika kipengele cha kioo cha float (aina ya 7005), kutotozwa ushuru kwa bidhaa kutoka nchi wanachama wa Jumuiya ya Afrika Mashariki zinazokidhi Kanuni za Asili ya Bidhaa kunaondolewa, ilhali msamaha kwa wasindikaji waliosajiliwa wanaopendekezwa na Waziri unabaki. Vipengele vipya vinavyoongezwa: bidhaa za plastiki zinazoagizwa (3923.30.00 na 3923.90.90), asilimia 10; magari ya kale, ya zamani na ya kawaida ya kihistoria, asilimia 50 ya thamani inayotozwa ushuru; MDF, mbao za chembe, block board, plywood na mbao za aina ya 4407.19.00 zinazoagizwa, kila kimoja asilimia 30; karatasi za bango zisizochapishwa, flex banner na karatasi za PVC zisizochapishwa (3921.12.10 na 3921.90.10), KSh 200 kwa kilo au asilimia 35 ya thamani inayotozwa ushuru; vichwa vya bafu (shower heads) vinavyoagizwa (8516.10) na vipengele vya kupasha joto vinavyotumika kutengeneza vichwa hivyo pekee, kila kimoja asilimia 35; bidhaa za tumbaku ya mdomoni zisizovutwa kama snus, KSh 2,000 kwa kilo; karatasi za plastiki zisizochapishwa (3920.43.10), asilimia 10; na pre-personal chip modules (8542.31.00), asilimia 10. Katika Sehemu ya II: katika aya ya 4A, maneno "deposited into a customer's betting wallet" yanakuwa "deposited for betting purposes", na sharti la aya ya 4A linafutwa. Katika aya ya 4B, maneno hayo yanakuwa "deposited for gambling purposes". Katika aya ya 9, neno "service" linaingizwa kabla ya "providers". Katika Sehemu ya III: ufafanuzi wa "amount deposited into a customer's betting wallet" unafutwa. Ufafanuzi mpya wa "amount deposited" unaongezwa: jumla ya fedha au thamani ya fedha iliyolipwa, kuhamishwa, kuwekwa au kutolewa kwa ajili ya kubashiri au kucheza kamari kwa mtu mwenye leseni chini ya Sheria ya Udhibiti wa Kamari, iwe imetoka kwa mchezaji au mwendeshaji, kwa fedha taslimu au vitu vinavyolingana nazo, iwe imehifadhiwa kwenye akaunti au la, au imegeuzwa kuwa chips, tokeni, tiketi au krediti. Ufafanuzi wa "virtual asset" na "virtual asset service provider" unaongezwa, ukichukua maana iliyo katika kifungu cha 2 cha Sheria ya Watoa Huduma za Mali Pepe, 2025.
explanation.sheng: Section 36 ina-amend First Schedule ya Excise Duty Act, ambayo ina-list goods na services na excise duty ya kila moja. Description ya zamani ya fruit juices na vegetable juice ina-delete, na inaingia entries mbili mpya: juice bila added sugar ni KSh 14.14 per litre, na juice na added sugar au sweetener ni KSh 20 per litre. clauses.heading: Insertion of a new section 6C in Cap. 469B.
clauses.text: 39.The Tax Procedures Act is amended by inserting the following new sections immediately after section 6B- Vir1ua1 asset service 6C. (1) Each virtual asset service providers to file information returns. provider shall file an information return with the Commissioner in respect of all the virtual-asset users with which it maintains a relationship in every calendar year and that are identified as reportable users or as having controlling persons that are reportable persons. (2) The information return under this section shall contain only such information as is necessary, relevant and proportionate Cap.41JC for the purposes of compliance with this Act and any agreement entered into under section 6D, and shall be collected, processed, retained and disclosed in accordance with the Data Protection Act. (3) A virtual asset provider shall be required to file the information return under subsection (1) if the virtual asset service provider provides a service that effectuates exchange transactions or making available a trading platform on behalf of a customer, and includes acting as a counterparty, or as an intermediary, to the exchange transactions. (4) A person who makes a false statement in an information return under subsection ( 1) commits an offence and shall be liable on conviction to a fine of one hundred thousand shillings for each false statement, or imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years, or to both. (5) A person who omits any information required to be included in an information return under subsection (1), shall be liable to a penalty of one hundred thousand shillings for each omission. (6) A person shall not be liable under subsection (4) or (5) where the information required to be included in an information return under subsection (1) is in respect of another person and a reasonable effort was made by the person to obtain the information from that other person. (7) A virtual asset service provider that fails to file an information return or a "nil" information return when required under subsection (1) shall be liable to pay a penalty of one million shillings for each failure. Agreements for the 6D. (1) Kenya may enter into an automatic exchange agreement with another country for the of information with other countries on automatic exchange of information relating virtual asset transactions. to transactions involving virtual assets. (2) An agreement under subsection (1) shall provide for the exchange of information relating to- (a) information returns filed under section 6C (l); (b) due diligence reporting and record keeping obligations prescribed under this section; ( c) the virtual asset users with which a virtual asset service provider maintains a relationship in every calendar year and that are identified as reportable users or as having controlling persons that are reportable persons; (d) nil return filings by virtual asset service providers who do not maintain a relationship with virtual asset users that are identified as reportable users or as having controlling persons that are reportable persons; and (e) arrangements or practices by virtual asset service providers, the main purpose or one of the main purposes of which can reasonably be considered to be to avoid obligations imposed under this Act. (3) The information exchanged pursuant to an agreement under this section shall- Cap. 4JIC (a) be in accordance with the Data Protection Act; and (b) be limited to information that is necessary, relevant and proportionate for the purposes specified in the applicable agreement. (4 ) The Commissioner shall not exchange information under this section unless he is satisfied that the receiving jurisdiction maintains adequate legal, technical and organisational safeguards for the protection of personal information. (5) The Commissioner shall maintain a record of all disclosures made under this section, including the receiving jurisdiction, date of disclosure, legal basis of disclosure and categories of information disclosed. ( 6)In this section - "information returil" means a report, setting out prescribed information which a reporting virtual-asset service provider is required to file with the Commissioner. (7) The Cabinet Secretary may make regulations necessary for the implementation of this section.

explanation.en: This section adds two new sections to the Tax Procedures Act: 6C and 6D. Under 6C, each virtual asset service provider (a business that carries out exchange transactions or runs a trading platform for customers) must file a yearly information return with the Commissioner on its users who are reportable, or whose controlling persons are reportable. The return may hold only information that is necessary, relevant and proportionate, handled under the Data Protection Act. A false statement is an offence with a fine of KSh 100,000 per statement, up to three years in prison, or both; each omission carries a KSh 100,000 penalty, and failing to file an information return (including a nil return) carries a KSh 1 million penalty per failure, but there is no liability if a reasonable effort was made to get the information from the other person. Under 6D, Kenya may sign agreements with other countries to automatically exchange information on virtual asset transactions, and the Commissioner may share information only if satisfied the other country has adequate safeguards for personal information, and must keep a record of each disclosure.
explanation.sw: Kifungu hiki kinaongeza vifungu viwili vipya katika Sheria ya Taratibu za Kodi: 6C na 6D. Kwa mujibu wa 6C, kila mtoa huduma wa mali pepe (biashara inayofanya miamala ya kubadilishana mali pepe au kuendesha jukwaa la biashara kwa wateja) anatakiwa kuwasilisha kwa Kamishna ripoti ya taarifa kila mwaka kuhusu watumiaji wake wanaoripotiwa, au ambao watu wanaowadhibiti wanaripotiwa. Taarifa hizo lazima ziwe zile tu zinazohitajika, zinazohusika na zinazolingana na madhumuni, na zishughulikiwe kwa mujibu wa Sheria ya Ulinzi wa Data. Taarifa ya uongo ni kosa lenye faini ya shilingi 100,000 kwa kila taarifa, au kifungo cha hadi miaka mitatu, au vyote viwili; kila taarifa iliyoachwa ina adhabu ya shilingi 100,000, na kutowasilisha ripoti (hata ripoti tupu) kuna adhabu ya shilingi milioni moja kwa kila kosa, ila hakuna dhima iwapo juhudi za busara zilifanywa kupata taarifa kutoka kwa mtu mwingine. Kwa mujibu wa 6D, Kenya inaweza kuingia makubaliano na nchi nyingine ya kubadilishana taarifa kiotomatiki kuhusu miamala ya mali pepe, na Kamishna anaweza kushiriki taarifa tu akiridhika kwamba nchi inayopokea ina ulinzi wa kutosha wa taarifa binafsi, na lazima atunze kumbukumbu ya kila ufichuzi.
explanation.sheng: Section hii ina-add two new sections kwa Tax Procedures Act: 6C na 6D. Kwa 6C, kila virtual asset service provider (company inayofanya exchange transactions au ku-run trading platform kwa customers) ana-required ku-file information return na Commissioner kila year, kuhusu users wake ambao ni reportable, au ambao controlling persons wao ni reportable. Information iwe necessary, relevant na proportionate, na ihandliwe kulingana na Data Protection Act. False statement ni offence: fine ya KSh 100,000 kwa kila statement, au jail term ya hadi three years, au both; kila omission ina penalty ya KSh 100,000, na ku-fail ku-file information return (hata nil return) ni penalty ya KSh 1 million kwa kila failure, ila hakuna liability kama reasonable effort ilifanywa kupata information kutoka kwa the other person. Kwa 6D, Kenya inaweza ku-sign agreement na another country ya automatic exchange ya information kuhusu virtual asset transactions, na Commissioner anaweza ku-share information tu kama ame-satisfy kwamba country hiyo ina safeguards za ku-protect personal information, na lazima aku-keep record ya kila disclosure.

Where the Commissioner finds that a person entered a scheme to get a tax benefit, the Commissioner may work out that person's tax as if the scheme had never happened. The Commissioner must rely on information submitted or obtained under the listed laws and systems, issue an assessment within five years from the last day of the tax period, and give written reasons within thirty days. explanation.sw: Kifungu hiki kinaongeza kifungu kipya cha 18A kwenye Sheria ya Taratibu za Kodi kuhusu mipango ya kukwepa kodi. Kamishna akiamua kwamba mtu aliingia katika mpango ili kupata faida ya kodi, anaweza kukokotoa deni la kodi la mtu huyo kana kwamba mpango huo haukufanyika. Kamishna lazima atumie taarifa zilizowasilishwa au kupatikana chini ya sheria na mifumo iliyotajwa, atoe tathmini ndani ya miaka mitano tangu siku ya mwisho ya kipindi cha kodi husika, na atoe sababu kwa maandishi ndani ya siku thelathini. Mlipakodi anaweza kuomba uamuzi wa kibinafsi (private ruling) kuhusu miamala changamano, na maneno "mpango" (kwa mfano mkataba au pendekezo) na "faida ya kodi" (kwa mfano kodi ya chini, marejesho au kuchelewesha malipo) yamefafanuliwa kwa upana.

Kama Commissioner ataona person ameingia kwa scheme ili apate tax benefit, anaweza ku-calculate tax ya huyo person kama scheme haikuwahi happen. Commissioner anatumia information iliyo-submitted under sheria na systems zilizo-listed, ana-issue assessment within five years from last day ya tax period, na ana-give written reasons within thirty days. Taxpayer anaweza ku-apply for private ruling kwa complex transactions, na "scheme" na "tax benefit" zime-defined broadly, kama plan au agreement, na lower tax, refund au delayed payment.

clauses.heading: Insertion of new 23B section in Cap. 469B.
clauses.text: 43.The Tax Procedure Act is amended by inserting the new section immediately after section 23A - Production of 23B. (1) A person who imports, or Export Declaration claims to have imported goods into Kenya for imported goods. shall obtain and retain an export declaration, export entry, custom export certificate or such other customs document issued by the competent authority in the country of export evidencing the lawful exportation of the goods from that country. (2)The export declaration or such other document referred to in subsection (1) shall contain such particulars as may be prescribed including- (a) the name and address of the exporter; (b) the name and address of the importer; (c) a description of the goods exported; (d) the quality, value and tariff classification of the goods; (e) the country of export and country of destination; (f) the date of exportation; and (g) the reference number assigned by the customs authority of the country of export. (3) An importer shall retain the export declaration and supporting documents for a period of five years from the date of importation and shall produce the documents upon request by the Commissioner. (4) Where an importer fails to produce an export declaration or other satisfactory evidence of exportation from the country of origin or export, the Commissioner may- (a) reject any claim relating to the importation, value, origin, cost or ownership of the goods; (b) determine the customs value, tax liability or any claim for deduction, exemption, refund or relief on the basis of the information available to the Commissioner; and (c ) impose such administrative penalties as may be prescribed. (5) The Commissioner may waive the requirement for production of an export declaration where the customs administration of the country of export does not issue export declarations for the category of goods. (6) The Cabinet Secretary may make regulations to provide for the form, manner of production, categories of acceptable export declarations and equivalent customs documents for purposes of this section.

explanation.en: This section adds a new section 23B to the Tax Procedures Act. Anyone who imports goods into Kenya, or claims to have imported them, must get and keep a document from the exporting country's customs (such as an export declaration) showing the goods were lawfully exported. The document must carry details such as the exporter and importer names and addresses, a description, quality, value and tariff classification of the goods, the countries involved, the date and a reference number. The importer keeps it for five years and produces it when the Commissioner asks. If it is not produced, the Commissioner may reject claims about the goods, set the customs value and tax from the information available, and impose prescribed penalties. The Commissioner may waive the requirement where the exporting country does not issue export declarations for that category of goods, and the Cabinet Secretary may make regulations on the form and acceptable documents.
explanation.sw: Kifungu hiki kinaongeza kifungu kipya cha 23B kwenye Sheria ya Taratibu za Kodi. Yeyote anayeingiza bidhaa nchini Kenya, au anayedai kuziingiza, lazima apate na ahifadhi hati kutoka forodha ya nchi ya mauzo ya nje (kama tamko la mauzo ya nje) inayoonyesha bidhaa zilisafirishwa kihalali. Hati hiyo ina maelezo kama majina na anwani za muuzaji na mwagizaji, maelezo ya bidhaa, ubora, thamani na uainishaji wa ushuru, nchi husika, tarehe na nambari ya kumbukumbu. Mwagizaji anaihifadhi kwa miaka mitano na kuiwasilisha Kamishna akiomba. Asipoiwasilisha, Kamishna anaweza kukataa madai kuhusu bidhaa, kuamua thamani ya forodha na kodi kwa kutumia taarifa alizonazo, na kutoza adhabu zilizowekwa. Kamishna anaweza kuondoa sharti hilo ikiwa nchi ya mauzo haitoi matamko kwa aina hiyo ya bidhaa, na Waziri anaweza kutunga kanuni kuhusu fomu na hati zinazokubalika.
explanation.sheng: Section hii ina-add section mpya 23B kwa Tax Procedures Act. Anyone anayeimport goods Kenya, au anayesema ameimport, lazima apate na ana-keep export declaration kutoka customs ya country iliyo-export goods, inayo-show goods ziliexportiwa legally, na ina details kama names na addresses za exporter na importer, description, value, tariff classification, countries, date na reference number. Importer ana-keep documents kwa five years na ku-produce Commissioner akiomba, na akikosa, Commissioner anaweza ku-reject claims kuhusu goods, ku-decide customs value na tax kutoka information aliyonayo, na ku-impose penalties. Commissioner anaweza pia ku-waive requirement kama country ya export haitoi export declarations kwa hizo goods, na Cabinet Secretary anaweza ku-make regulations kuhusu form na documents zinazokubalika.

neutral_check.note: Described the documents, retention period and Commissioner's powers as written, with no opinion, advice or view on legality.

clauses.text: 44. The Tax Procedures Act is amended by inserting the following new section immediately after section 29- Commissioner to 29A . ( 1) The Commissioner may, in issue an assessment. accordance with the information obtained in accordance with subsection (2), issue an assessment on the income of a person as he may deem necessary. (2)The Commissioner shall rely on- ( a) the information submitted to the Cap.470 Commissioner under section 35(5) of the Income Tax Act; (b) the accounting of tax deducted under section 37(1) of the Income Tax Act; Cap. 469. (c) the information submitted to the Commissioner under section 5A of the Kenya Revenue Authority Act; Cap. 469B. (d) the information submitted to the electronic system established under section 23A of the Tax Procedures Act; (e) the information submitted to the Commissioner under section 24A; (f) the information obtained from the inspection of goods and records conducted under section 58; (g) the information obtained from the auditing of the records produced under section 59; (h) the information submitted to the data management and reporting system established under section 59A; or (i) the information submitted to the Commissioner under written law, to issue an assessment under subsection (1). (3) The Commissioner may request the taxpayer to provide the relevant information in writing at least thirty days before issuance of an assessment under subsection (1). (4) The taxpayer may object to an assessment under this section in accordance with section 51 of this Act.

explanation.en: This adds a new section 29A to the Tax Procedures Act. It lets the Commissioner issue an assessment (a formal calculation of a person's income for tax purposes) based on information already obtained. The Commissioner must rely on these sources: information submitted under section 35(5) of the Income Tax Act, records of tax deducted under section 37(1) of that Act, information under section 5A of the Kenya Revenue Authority Act, the electronic system under section 23A and information under section 24A of the Tax Procedures Act, inspections of goods and records (section 58), audits of records (section 59), the data management and reporting system (section 59A), and information submitted under any other written law. The Commissioner may ask the taxpayer in writing for relevant information at least thirty days before issuing the assessment, and the taxpayer may object to the assessment under section 51.
explanation.sw: Kifungu hiki kinaongeza kifungu kipya cha 29A kwenye Sheria ya Taratibu za Kodi. Kinamruhusu Kamishna kutoa tathmini ya mapato ya mtu (hesabu rasmi ya mapato kwa madhumuni ya kodi) kwa kutegemea taarifa alizokwisha zipata. Kamishna atategemea taarifa kutoka vyanzo hivi: taarifa zilizowasilishwa chini ya kifungu cha 35(5) cha Sheria ya Kodi ya Mapato, rekodi za kodi iliyokatwa chini ya kifungu cha 37(1) cha sheria hiyo, taarifa chini ya kifungu cha 5A cha Sheria ya Mamlaka ya Mapato ya Kenya, mfumo wa kielektroniki wa kifungu cha 23A na taarifa chini ya kifungu cha 24A vya Sheria ya Taratibu za Kodi, ukaguzi wa bidhaa na rekodi (kifungu cha 58), ukaguzi wa hesabu za rekodi (kifungu cha 59), mfumo wa usimamizi wa data na utoaji wa ripoti (kifungu cha 59A), na taarifa zilizowasilishwa chini ya sheria nyingine yoyote iliyoandikwa. Kamishna anaweza kumwomba mlipakodi taarifa husika kwa maandishi angalau siku thelathini kabla ya kutoa tathmini, na mlipakodi anaweza kupinga tathmini hiyo chini ya kifungu cha 51.
explanation.sheng: Section hii ina-add new section 29A kwa Tax Procedures Act. Ina-allow Commissioner ku-issue assessment (calculation rasmi ya income ya mtu kwa ajili ya tax) based on information ambayo ako nayo tayari. Commissioner ana-rely on information kutoka sources hizi: information submitted under section 35(5) ya Income Tax Act, records za tax deducted under section 37(1) ya Income Tax Act, information under section 5A ya Kenya Revenue Authority Act, electronic system ya section 23A na information under section 24A ya Tax Procedures Act, inspection ya goods na records (section 58), audit ya records (section 59), data management and reporting system (section 59A), na information yoyote submitted under written law nyingine. Commissioner anaweza ku-request information kutoka kwa taxpayer in writing at least thirty days kabla ya assessment, na taxpayer anaweza ku-object kwa assessment under section 51.

neutral_check.note: Describes the new assessment power, the listed information sources, the thirty-day written request and the right to object, with no opinion or advice.

clauses.heading: Amendment of section 3 7E of Cap.469B.
clauses.text: 45.Section 37E of the Tax Procedures Act is amended- (a) in subsection (1), by deleting the expression "31st December, 2023" appearing immediately after the words "due before the" and substituting therefor the expression" 31st December, 2025"; (b) in subsection (2), by deleting the expression "31st December, 2023" appearing immediately after the words "paid before the" and substituting therefor the expression" 31st December, 2025"; (c) in subsection (3)- (i) in paragraph (a), by deleting the expression "31st December, 2023" appearing immediately after the words "up to the" and substituting therefor the expression "31st December, 2025"; (ii)in paragraph (b), by deleting the expression "30th June, 2025" appearing immediately after the words "later than the" and substituting therefor the expression· "31st December, 2026"; (d) in subsection (4)- (i) by deleting the expression "31st December, 2023" appearing immediately after the words "as on the" and substituting therefor the expression" 31st December, 2025"; (ii) by deleting the expression "30th June, 2025" appearing immediately after the words "unpaid on the" and substituting therefor the expression "31st December, 2026".

explanation.en: Section 45 changes dates in section 37E of the Tax Procedures Act. The date 31st December 2023 becomes 31st December 2025 in subsections (1), (2), (3)(a) and (4). The date 30th June 2025 becomes 31st December 2026 in subsections (3)(b) and (4). Only the dates change, nothing else in section 37E.
explanation.sw: Kifungu cha 45 kinabadilisha tarehe katika kifungu cha 37E cha Sheria ya Taratibu za Kodi (Tax Procedures Act). Tarehe 31 Desemba 2023 inabadilishwa kuwa 31 Desemba 2025 katika vifungu vidogo vya (1), (2), (3)(a) na (4). Tarehe 30 Juni 2025 inabadilishwa kuwa 31 Desemba 2026 katika vifungu vidogo vya (3)(b) na (4). Hakuna badiliko lingine katika kifungu cha 37E.
explanation.sheng: Section 45 ina-change dates kwa section 37E ya Tax Procedures Act. Ile date ya 31st December 2023 sasa ni 31st December 2025 kwa subsections (1), (2), (3)(a) na (4). Ile ya 30th June 2025 ina-become 31st December 2026 kwa subsections (3)(b) na (4). Ni dates tu zina-change, hakuna kitu kingine kwa section 37E.

neutral_check.note: Date-only amendment, described as written with no opinion, advice or legal judgement.

clauses.heading: Insertion of new section 39B in Cap.469B
clauses.text: 46.The Tax Procedure Act is amended by inserting the new section immediately after section 39 A- couectorto recover 39B. (1) Notwithstanding the provisions unpaid amount under of any other wntten law' where the other laws Commissioner is the Collector of a fees, levy or charge under any other written law, the Commissioner may recover any unpaid amount of the fee, levy or charge as if it was an unpaid tax under a tax law. (2) Subject to sub-section (1), where the amount of the unpaid fee, levy or charge does not exceed one hundred thousand shillings it shall be recoverable summarily.

explanation.en: Section 46 adds a new section 39B to the Tax Procedures Act. Where the Commissioner is the collector of a fee, levy or charge under any other law, the Commissioner can recover an unpaid amount as if it were an unpaid tax under a tax law. If the unpaid amount is KSh 100,000 or less, it can be recovered summarily, which means through a quicker and simpler procedure.
explanation.sw: Kifungu cha 46 kinaongeza kifungu kipya cha 39B kwenye Sheria ya Taratibu za Kodi. Pale ambapo Kamishna ndiye mkusanyaji wa ada, tozo au malipo chini ya sheria nyingine, Kamishna anaweza kurejesha kiasi ambacho hakijalipwa kana kwamba ni kodi isiyolipwa chini ya sheria ya kodi. Kama kiasi hicho hakizidi shilingi laki moja (KSh 100,000), kinaweza kurejeshwa kwa njia ya muhtasari, yaani utaratibu wa haraka na rahisi zaidi.
explanation.sheng: Section 46 ina-add section mpya 39B kwa Tax Procedures Act. Kama Commissioner ni collector wa fee, levy au charge chini ya sheria nyingine, anaweza ku-recover unpaid amount kama ni unpaid tax chini ya tax law. Kama unpaid amount ni KSh 100,000 or less, anaweza ku-recover hiyo pesa summarily, yaani kwa quick and simple process.

neutral_check.note: Described only what the new section does: who can recover, what is recovered, and the KSh 100,000 summary threshold. No opinion, advice or legal verdict.

clauses.heading: Amendment of section 7 5 of Cap. 469B.
clauses.text: 47.Section 75 of the Tax Procedures Act is amended by adding the following new section immediately after subsection (2)- (3) The Commissioner may use the information technology contemplated under subsection ( 1) to generate a prepo pulated tax return on behalf of a person required to submit or lodge a tax return. (4) The Commissioner shall notify the person that a pre-populated return has been issued under sub-section (3). (5) The pre-populated return issued under subsection (3) shall be issued on or before end of January of each year of income to the person required to submit or lodge a return. (6) A person who is issued with a prepopulated return under subsection (3) may confirm or amend the pre-populated the return. (7)A person shall confirm or amend the prepopulated return within two months from the date the pre-populated return is issued by the Commissioner. (8)A person required to submit or lodge a tax return may rely on the pre-populated return generated by the Commissioner under subsection (3)to submit or lodge the return.

explanation.en: This section adds new subsections (3) to (8) to section 75 of the Tax Procedures Act. The Commissioner may use information technology to prepare a pre-populated tax return, which is a return already filled in with details, for a person who has to file one. The Commissioner must notify the person, and the return must be issued on or before the end of January of each year of income. The person may confirm or amend it within two months from the date it is issued, and may rely on it to file their return.
explanation.sw: Kifungu hiki kinaongeza vifungu vidogo vipya (3) hadi (8) kwenye kifungu cha 75 cha Sheria ya Taratibu za Kodi. Kamishna anaweza kutumia teknolojia ya habari kuandaa ritani ya kodi iliyojazwa awali, yaani ritani yenye maelezo tayari, kwa mtu anayetakiwa kuwasilisha ritani. Kamishna lazima amjulishe mtu huyo, na ritani hiyo hutolewa kabla au ifikapo mwisho wa Januari ya kila mwaka wa mapato. Mtu huyo anaweza kuithibitisha au kuirekebisha ndani ya miezi miwili tangu ilipotolewa, na anaweza kuitegemea kuwasilisha ritani yake.
explanation.sheng: Section 47 ina-add subsections mpya (3) hadi (8) kwa section 75 ya Tax Procedures Act. Commissioner anaweza ku-use information technology ku-generate pre-populated return (return ambayo tayari ina details ndani) kwa person anayetakiwa ku-file return. Commissioner ana-notify huyo person, na return inatolewa on or before end ya January ya kila year of income. Person anaweza ku-confirm au ku-amend return hiyo within two months from the date ilipotolewa, na pia anaweza kuitegemea ku-file return yake.

neutral_check.note: Describes only what the new subsections do. The section applies to all persons who must file returns, so no group is tagged.

clauses.heading: Repeal and replacement of section 86 of Cap. 469B.
clauses.text: 48.The Tax Procedures Act is amended by repealing section 86 and replacing it with the following new section- Failure to comply 86. (1) Where the Commissioner with electronic tax determines that a taxpayer has failed to system. comply with the requirement under a tax law to issue an electronic tax invoice, submit a tax return in electronic form, or pay tax electronically pursuant to section 75, the Commissioner shall issue a notice in writing to the taxpayer requiring the taxpayer to provide reasons for the non-compliance. (2) Upon receipt of the response of the taxpayer as required under subsection (1), the Commissioner shall consider whether- (a) the failure to comply arose from circumstances beyond the reasonable control of the taxpayer; (b) the failure to comply was not due to the wilful neglect or deliberate default of the taxpayer, and (c ) the taxpayer took reasonable steps to comply with the relevant requirement as soon as practicable. (3) Where the Commissioner is not satisfied by the reasons given under subsection (2), the taxpayer shall be liable to pay the higher of the following penalties- (a) five percent of the tax due; (b) one hundred thousand shillings, in the case of a company; or (c) in the case of an individual, ten thousand shillings.

explanation.en: This section replaces section 86 of the Tax Procedures Act, which deals with failure to use the electronic tax system. If the Commissioner finds that a taxpayer did not issue an electronic tax invoice, file a return electronically, or pay tax electronically as required, the Commissioner sends a written notice asking for reasons. The Commissioner then considers whether the failure was beyond the taxpayer's reasonable control, was not wilful neglect or deliberate default, and whether the taxpayer took reasonable steps to comply as soon as practicable. If the Commissioner is not satisfied with the reasons, the taxpayer pays whichever is higher: 5% of the tax due, or a fixed amount of 100,000 shillings for a company or 10,000 shillings for an individual.
explanation.sw: Kifungu hiki kinabadilisha kifungu cha 86 cha Sheria ya Taratibu za Kodi, kinachohusu kushindwa kutumia mfumo wa kielektroniki wa kodi. Kamishna akibaini kuwa mlipakodi hakutoa ankara ya kodi ya kielektroniki, hakuwasilisha marejesho ya kodi kielektroniki, au hakulipa kodi kielektroniki kama inavyotakiwa, anatuma notisi ya maandishi akitaka sababu za kutotii. Kisha Kamishna anazingatia kama kushindwa huko kulitokana na mazingira yaliyo nje ya uwezo wa mlipakodi, kama hakukutokana na uzembe wa makusudi au kosa la kimakusudi, na kama mlipakodi alichukua hatua zinazofaa kutii mapema iwezekanavyo. Kamishna asiporidhika na sababu hizo, mlipakodi hulipa adhabu iliyo kubwa zaidi kati ya asilimia tano ya kodi inayodaiwa, au kiasi maalum cha shilingi laki moja kwa kampuni au shilingi elfu kumi kwa mtu binafsi.
explanation.sheng: Section 48 ina-replace section 86 ya Tax Procedures Act, inayohusu failure ya ku-comply na electronic tax system. Kama Commissioner anaona taxpayer hakuissue electronic tax invoice, hakufile return electronically, au hakupay tax electronically kama ilivyo required, ana-send notice in writing ya kuomba reasons. Kisha ana-check kama failure ilitokana na mambo nje ya control ya taxpayer, kama haikuwa on purpose (neglect au deliberate default), na kama taxpayer alijaribu ku-comply asap. Kama Commissioner hana-accept reasons, taxpayer ana-pay penalty iliyo juu kati ya 5% ya tax due na fixed amount: 100,000 shillings kwa company au 10,000 shillings kwa individual.

neutral_check.note: Describes the notice, the three points the Commissioner considers and the penalty amounts as written, with no opinion or advice. Applies to all taxpayers equally, so no group is tagged.

clauses.heading: Amendment of section 89 of Cap. 469B.
clauses.text: 49.Section 89 of the Tax Procedures Act is amended- (a) in subsection (5A)- (i) in paragraph (c), by deleting the words "due to a malfunction of an electronic tax system" appearing immediately after the word "interest"; (ii) by inserting the following new paragraph immediately after paragraph (c )- (ca) a malfunction of an electronic tax system; (b) by inserting the following new subsection immediately after subsection (5A)- (5B) Despite subsection (5A), the Commissioner may waive the whole or part of any penalty or interest imposed under this Act where the liability to pay the penalty or interest does not exceed two million shillings and was due to an error generated by an electronic tax system.

explanation.en: This section changes the part of the Tax Procedures Act that lets the Commissioner waive penalties and interest. The words about a malfunction of an electronic tax system are taken out of paragraph (c) and made their own paragraph, (ca), in subsection (5A). It also adds a new subsection (5B): the Commissioner may waive all or part of a penalty or interest of up to two million shillings if it was caused by an error generated by an electronic tax system.
explanation.sw: Kifungu hiki kinabadilisha sehemu ya Sheria ya Taratibu za Ushuru (Tax Procedures Act) inayomruhusu Kamishna kusamehe adhabu na riba. Maneno kuhusu hitilafu ya mfumo wa kielektroniki wa ushuru yanaondolewa kwenye aya (c) na kuwekwa katika aya yake mpya, (ca), ndani ya kifungu kidogo cha (5A). Pia kinaongeza kifungu kidogo kipya cha (5B): Kamishna anaweza kusamehe adhabu au riba yote au sehemu yake, ikiwa kiasi hakizidi shilingi milioni mbili na kilitokana na kosa lililozalishwa na mfumo wa kielektroniki wa ushuru.
explanation.sheng: Section hii ina-amend Tax Procedures Act, kwa part ambayo Commissioner anaweza ku-waive penalty na interest. Words kuhusu malfunction ya electronic tax system zina-move kutoka paragraph (c) na kuwa paragraph yao wenyewe, (ca), ndani ya subsection (5A). Pia ina-add subsection mpya (5B): Commissioner anaweza ku-waive penalty au interest all au part yake kama haizidi two million shillings na ilitokana na error from electronic tax system.

neutral_check.note: Describes only the drafting changes and the new waiver power with its two million shilling limit, with no opinion on policy or legality.

clauses.heading: Amendment to section 112 of Cap.469B.
clauses.text: 50.Section 112 of the Tax Procedures Act is amended in subsection (2) by inserting the following new paragraph immediately after paragraph (b) - (ba) the procedure for the submission or lodging of returns based on pre-populated tax returns generated by the Commissioner.

explanation.en: This section adds one new item, paragraph (ba), to the list in subsection (2) of section 112 of the Tax Procedures Act. The new item is the procedure for submitting or lodging returns that are based on pre-populated tax returns (returns the Commissioner has already filled in with information) generated by the Commissioner. It is a small technical amendment that adds an item to a list.
explanation.sw: Kifungu cha 50 kinarekebisha kifungu cha 112 cha Sheria ya Taratibu za Ushuru (Tax Procedures Act). Kinaongeza kipengele kipya (ba) kwenye orodha iliyo katika kifungu kidogo cha (2). Kipengele hicho kinahusu utaratibu wa kuwasilisha marejesho ya ushuru yanayotegemea marejesho yaliyojazwa awali na Kamishna kwa taarifa tayari. Ni marekebisho madogo ya kiufundi ya kuongeza kipengele kwenye orodha.
explanation.sheng: Section 50 ina-amend section 112 ya Tax Procedures Act. Ina-add item mpya, paragraph (ba), kwa list iliyo kwa subsection (2). Item hiyo ni procedure ya ku-submit returns zinazotumia pre-populated tax returns, yaani returns ambazo Commissioner ame-generate na zina information tayari. Ni technical amendment ndogo ya kuongeza item kwa list.

neutral_check.note: Describes only a small technical addition to a list in section 112(2), with no opinion, advice or legal verdict.

clauses.heading: Amendment of section 9 of Cap. 469C.
clauses.text: 51.Section 9 of the Miscellaneous Fees and Levies Act is amended by deleting the words "import declaration fee, railway development levy and export levy" appearing immediately after the words "payment of' and substituting therefor the words "the fees and levies imposed under Part III".

explanation.en: Section 51 changes section 9 of the Miscellaneous Fees and Levies Act. It removes the words "import declaration fee, railway development levy and export levy" that come right after "payment of", and puts in "the fees and levies imposed under Part III". It is a wording change: instead of naming three charges one by one, section 9 now points to whatever fees and levies Part III imposes.
explanation.sw: Kifungu cha 51 kinarekebisha kifungu cha 9 cha Sheria ya Ada na Ushuru Mbalimbali (Miscellaneous Fees and Levies Act). Kinaondoa maneno "import declaration fee, railway development levy and export levy" yanayofuata maneno "payment of", na kuweka maneno "the fees and levies imposed under Part III". Ni mabadiliko ya maneno tu: badala ya kutaja ada tatu moja moja, kifungu cha 9 sasa kinarejelea ada na ushuru wowote unaotozwa chini ya Sehemu ya III.
explanation.sheng: Section 51 ina-amend section 9 ya Miscellaneous Fees and Levies Act. Ina-delete words "import declaration fee, railway development levy and export levy" zinazokuja baada ya "payment of", na ina-put "the fees and levies imposed under Part III". Ni change ya wording tu: badala ya ku-list three fees and levies, section 9 sasa ina-refer kwa fees and levies zote under Part III.

neutral_check.note: Small technical wording amendment described as it reads, with no opinion, advice or legal judgement.

clauses.heading: Amendment of the Second Schedule to Cap. 469C.
clauses.text: 52.The Second Schedule to the Miscellaneous Fees and Levies Act is amended- ( a) in Part A- (i) by deleting paragraph (xv) and substituting therefor the following new paragraph- (xv) all parts of chapter 88 and goods of tariff heading 8802.30.00 and 8802.40.00; (ii) by inserting the following new paragraph immediately after paragraph (xxxii)- (xxxiii) Goods used in the construction of liquefied petroleum gas storage tanks and related infrastructure: Provided that the investment in the construction of liquefied petroleum gas storage tanks and related infrastructure in Kenya amounts to at least five billion shillings and has been recommended by the Cabinet Secretary responsible for matters relating to energy. (b) in Part B- (i) by deleting paragraph (xiii) and substituting therefor the following new paragraph- (xiii) all parts of chapter 88 and goods of tariff heading 8802.30.00 and 8802.40.00; (ii) by inserting the following new paragraph immediately after paragraph (xviii)- (xix) Goods used in the construction of liquefied petroleum gas storage tanks and related infrastructure: Provided that the investment in the construction of liquefied petroleum gas storage tanks and related infrastructure in Kenya amounts to at least five billion shillings and has been recommended by the Cabinet Secretary responsible for matters relating to energy .

explanation.en: This section changes the lists of goods in Part A and Part B of the Second Schedule to the Miscellaneous Fees and Levies Act. In each part, it replaces one existing entry with a new entry covering all of chapter 88 of the tariff (aircraft and their parts) and tariff headings 8802.30.00 and 8802.40.00 (aeroplanes). In each part it also adds a new entry for goods used to build liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) storage tanks and related infrastructure. That entry applies only if the investment in Kenya is at least five billion shillings and the Cabinet Secretary for energy has recommended it.
explanation.sw: Kifungu hiki kinabadilisha orodha za bidhaa katika Sehemu A na Sehemu B za Jedwali la Pili la Sheria ya Ada na Ushuru Mbalimbali. Katika kila sehemu, kinafuta kipengele kimoja na kuweka kipya kinachojumuisha sehemu zote za sura ya 88 ya ushuru (ndege na vipuri vyake) pamoja na vichwa vya ushuru 8802.30.00 na 8802.40.00 (ndege aina ya aeroplane). Pia kinaongeza kipengele kipya cha bidhaa zinazotumika kujenga matangi ya kuhifadhi gesi ya petroli iliyoyeyushwa (LPG) na miundombinu inayohusiana. Kipengele hicho kinatumika tu kama uwekezaji nchini Kenya ni angalau shilingi bilioni tano na Waziri anayehusika na nishati ameupendekeza.
explanation.sheng: Section hii ina-amend Second Schedule ya Miscellaneous Fees and Levies Act, kwa Part A na Part B zote. Kwa kila part, ina-replace item moja na item mpya inayo-cover all parts za chapter 88 (aircraft na parts zake) na tariff headings 8802.30.00 na 8802.40.00 (aeroplanes). Pia ina-add item mpya ya goods zinazotumika kwa construction ya LPG (liquefied petroleum gas) storage tanks na infrastructure inayohusiana. Item hiyo inafanya kazi tu kama investment ya Kenya ni at least five billion shillings na Cabinet Secretary wa energy ame-recommend.

neutral_check.note: Describes only the two changes in each part (the replaced aircraft entry and the new LPG storage entry) and its conditions, with no opinion, advice or legal verdict.

clauses.heading: Amendment of section 11 of No. 2 of 2024.
clauses.text: 53.Section 11 of the Affordable Housing Act is amended in sub-section (4) by deleting paragraph (a) and substituting therefor the following new paragraph- ( a) up to two (2%) percent of the monies to the collector for the collection of the Levy as may be approved by the Cabinet Secretary for the time being responsible for the National Treasury on the recommendation of the Cabinet Secretary

explanation.en: This section replaces paragraph (a) of section 11(4) of the Affordable Housing Act with a new paragraph. The new paragraph says that up to 2% of the monies can go to the collector, for collecting the Affordable Housing Levy. The amount needs approval from the Cabinet Secretary responsible for the National Treasury, on the recommendation of the Cabinet Secretary.
explanation.sw: Sehemu hii inafuta aya ndogo (a) ya kifungu cha 11(4) cha Sheria ya Nyumba za Bei Nafuu na kuweka aya mpya. Aya hiyo mpya inasema kwamba hadi asilimia mbili (2%) ya fedha inaweza kupewa mkusanyaji kwa ajili ya kukusanya Ushuru huo. Kiasi hicho kinahitaji idhini ya Waziri anayehusika na Hazina ya Taifa, kwa pendekezo la Waziri.
explanation.sheng: Section hii ina-replace paragraph (a) ya section 11(4) ya Affordable Housing Act na paragraph mpya. Paragraph mpya inasema up to 2% ya monies inaweza kwenda kwa collector kwa ajili ya ku-collect Levy. Amount hiyo ina-need approval ya Cabinet Secretary wa National Treasury, kwa recommendation ya Cabinet Secretary.

neutral_check.note: Small technical amendment, described only by what it changes, with no opinion or advice.

clauses.heading: Amendment to section 96A of Cap.480.
clauses.text: 54.Section 96A of the Stamp Duty Act is amended in subsection (1) by inserting the following new paragraph immediately after paragraph (b)- (c) that the effect thereof is to convey or transfer a beneficial interest in property from a person or persons to the real estate investment trust.

explanation.en: Section 54 changes section 96A of the Stamp Duty Act. In subsection (1), it adds a new paragraph (c) straight after paragraph (b). The new paragraph covers a document whose effect is to move a beneficial interest in property (the right to benefit from the property, such as its use or income, even if someone else holds the legal title) from one or more people to a real estate investment trust.
explanation.sw: Kifungu cha 54 kinarekebisha kifungu cha 96A cha Sheria ya Stamp Duty. Katika kifungu kidogo cha (1), kinaongeza aya mpya (c) mara baada ya aya (b). Aya hiyo inahusu hati ambayo athari yake ni kuhamisha maslahi ya kunufaika (beneficial interest) katika mali kutoka kwa mtu mmoja au zaidi hadi kwa mfuko wa uwekezaji katika mali isiyohamishika (real estate investment trust).
explanation.sheng: Section 54 ina-amend section 96A ya Stamp Duty Act, kwa subsection (1). Ina-add new paragraph (c) baada ya paragraph (b). Paragraph hiyo ni ya document ambayo effect yake ni ku-transfer beneficial interest kutoka kwa one or more persons kwenda kwa real estate investment trust. Beneficial interest ni right ya ku-benefit kutoka property, hata kama title iko kwa someone else.

neutral_check.note: Describes only the added paragraph (c) and what the text says, with no opinion, advice or judgement. Does not state what the rest of section 96A does, since that text is not provided.

clauses.heading: Amendment of section 3 of Cap 427.
clauses.text: 55.Section 3 of the Road Maintenance Levy Fund Act is amended in subsection (2) by deleting the words "three shillings" and substituting therefor the words "one shilling and fifty cents.

explanation.en: Section 55 changes subsection (2) of section 3 of the Road Maintenance Levy Fund Act (Cap 427). It removes the words "three shillings" and puts in "one shilling and fifty cents". This is a change to one amount only, and nothing else in that section is changed.
explanation.sw: Kifungu cha 55 kinarekebisha kifungu kidogo cha (2) cha kifungu cha 3 cha Sheria ya Mfuko wa Ushuru wa Matengenezo ya Barabara (Road Maintenance Levy Fund Act, Sura ya 427). Kinafuta maneno "shilingi tatu" na kuweka "shilingi moja na senti hamsini". Ni badiliko la kiasi kimoja tu, na hakuna kingine kinachobadilishwa katika kifungu hicho.
explanation.sheng: Section 55 ina-amend Section 3(2) ya Road Maintenance Levy Fund Act (Cap 427) kwa ku-change amount moja tu: three shillings inakuwa one shilling and fifty cents. Hakuna change nyingine kwa section hiyo.

neutral_check.note: Small technical amendment replacing one amount; described only what the text does, with no opinion on the change.
